Crypto lender Nimbus accused by US regulator of misleading 90,000 savers

Published 2026-10-06 17:30 UTC

The US financial regulator has accused the crypto lender Nimbus Lending of misleading more than 90,000 savers in a $1.2bn scheme, in the latest crackdown on the crypto industry.

The Securities and Exchange Commission said Nimbus and its founder, Mark Ellery, promised returns of up to 14% a year through a product called Yield Vault, claiming the money was lent to institutional borrowers. Instead, the SEC alleges, deposits from new customers were used to pay existing ones, and Ellery diverted more than $40m.

Nimbus froze customer withdrawals in August. Ellery's lawyers said he denied wrongdoing. Consumer groups said the case showed the need for tougher rules on crypto lending platforms.
